title: Linked List Cycle
summary: Return whether repeatedly following next links can revisit the same node.

contractDetails.constraints: 0–10,000 nodes with values in [−100,000, 100,000]. pos is −1 or a valid node index. Node identity determines revisiting, even when two values are equal.

statement: Return whether repeatedly following next links can revisit the same node. The judge uses pos only to build the input. When pos is nonnegative, the final node points to the node at that zero-based index. Otherwise the final node points to null. Your function receives only the head.

examples.explanation: The equal values belong to different nodes and the chain ends.
The only node points to itself.

constraints: 0–10,000 nodes with values in [−100,000, 100,000]. pos is −1 or a valid node index. Node identity determines revisiting, even when two values are equal.
hints: Conceptual: Values alone cannot tell you whether you have visited the same node twice.
Directional: Advance two pointers at different speeds.
Implementation: Move one pointer one step and the other two steps. A shared node means a cycle. A null fast pointer or successor means the chain ends.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. After both pointers enter a cycle, their distance changes by one on each step.
